title: Time lapse recording of cortical interneuron migration in mouse organotypic brain slices and explants
protocol: Prepare a 2%–4% agarose solution for brain embedding by adding 0.5 g to 1 g of low-melting agarose into a 50 mL conical tube containing 25 mL of sterile HBSS.
Transfer the tube into a microwave and bring the solution to boil.
Keep the tube cap loose until the agarose is completely dissolved.
Stop the microwave when the solution starts to boil, close the tube, and mix by inverting several times.
Repeat heating until complete dissolution of the agarose.
Transfer the tube into a 37°C incubator.
Allow the solution to cool down for approximately 20 minutes with the cap loose to release air bubbles.
Disinfect the abdomen of the pregnant female with a 70% alcoholic solution.
Open the abdomen using fine scissors under a laminar flow hood.
Collect the uterus and excise the embryos from the amniotic sac using forceps.
Harvest the embryos in sterile ice-cold HBSS immediately after dissection.
Section the head to dissect the embryonic brain.
Pour the low-melting agarose solution cooled to 37°C into a petri dish.
Transfer brains into the agarose solution using a perforated spoon.
Remove excess HBSS from the spoon using Tork® paper.
Rotate brains with forceps until olfactory bulbs face the bottom of the petri-dish and hindbrain is at the top.
Place the petri-dish on ice.
Rectify brain position with forceps until agarose solution is solid enough to maintain brains.
Allow agarose block to solidify on ice for 20 minutes.
Prepare MatTek® dish under cell culture hood by adding 1.6 mL of culture medium.
Install millicell membrane with sterile forceps at an angle of 30° to prevent air bubbles.
Transfer the dish into an incubator set at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Fill the vibratome tray with ice-cold HBSS and surround the tray with ice.
Set the section thickness to 300 μm, speed to 3, and frequency to 3.
Cut the agarose block using a razor blade into a truncated pyramid shape.
Position the block in the vibratome tray with the ventral part facing the blade.
Glue the agarose block on its major base on the vibratome support.
Ensure that the olfactory bulbs face upward.
Place the support with the brain in the vibratome tray.
Position the ventral part of the brain facing the blade of the vibratome.
Start slicing from rostral (olfactory bulbs) to caudal (hindbrain) regions.
Cut several brains at the same time, ensuring they fit within the size of the razor blade.
Obtain medial to caudal brain slices.
Collect brain slices with a spatula without detaching tissue from surrounding agarose.
Transfer the slices onto a millicell insert.
Place the dish in an incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Keep adding ice around the tray during the procedure.
Focus on interneuron migratory streams in the cortex using a 20× long-range objective.
Set the parameters of the confocal microscope to 37°C and 5% CO2.
Acquire time-lapse images.
Image at least 5 Z-steps of 2 μm every 5 min for 5 to 10 h.
Mix 5 mL of pre-polymer with 45 mL of catalyst in a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 3 mL of Chinese ink and mix with a spatula.
Place the tube on a 360°C vertical shaker for 30 min.
Centrifuge at 120 xg for 5 min.
Pour 25 mL of the solution into two 100 × 17 mm petri-dishes.
Place the dishes in a vacuum bell for 1 hour to remove bubbles.
Remove remaining bubbles with a micropipette tip if necessary.
Heat the dishes at 60°C for a minimum of 5 hours.
Clean the dishes with ethanol 70% after use.
Rinse the cleaned dishes with water and let them dry.
Prepare plasmid solution at 1 μg/μL in PBS with 0.05% Fast Green for a total volume of 15 μL.
Pull glass microcapillaries using a P-97 Flaming/Brown type Micropipette Puller.
Set heat to 634, pull to 92, velocity to 115, and time to 210.
Coat the glass-bottom dish with 0.1 mg/mL poly-L-ornithine diluted in sterile water.
Add 200 μL of poly-L-ornithine per compartment.
Incubate the dish at 37°C with 5% CO2 for 45 min.
Wash the dish compartments three times with sterile water.
Dilute laminin in sterile ice-cold PBS to reach a final concentration of 5 μg/mL.
Add 200 μL of laminin per compartment and incubate at 37°C for 2 h.
Alternatively, incubate laminin up to 24 h at 37°C.
Wash the dish compartments three times with sterile PBS.
Place the dish with PBS back into the 37°C incubator.
Sacrifice the E13.5 wild-type pregnant female by cervical dislocation followed by decapitation to confirm death.
Disinfect the abdomen of the pregnant female with a 70% alcoholic solution.
Open the abdomen with fine scissors under a laminar flow hood.
Extract the uterus and excise the embryos from the amniotic sac using forceps.
Harvest the embryos in sterile ice-cold HBSS immediately after extraction.
Section the heads of the embryos.
Dissect the brains from the sectioned heads.
Clean the brains from meninges as much as possible without damaging cortices.
Separate cortices from ganglionic eminences using forceps and micro knife.
Transfer cortices into one sterile Eppendorf® tube filled with HBSS and keep on ice.
Replace HBSS in the Eppendorf® tube with 800 μL of cold culture medium under a culture hood.
Mechanically dissociate the embryo cortices by pipetting up and down approximately 20 times.
Filtrate the dissociated cells through a sterile 40 μm cell strainer.
Replace PBS from coated dishes with 200 μl of dissociated cells per compartment.
Place the dish back into an incubator set to 37°C and 5% CO2 and let the cells adhere for 2 h.
During adherence, bring the temperature of the culture medium to 37°C.
Slowly add 600 μL of heated culture medium to each compartment without detaching adhered cells.
Maintain the dish in an incubator set to 37°C and 5% CO2 until the next day.
Fill a microcapillary with 10 μl of plasmid solution using microloader tips.
Cut approximately 2 mm of the capillary tip using small spring scissors.
Place the capillary on the Femtojet microinjector station and set the parameters: Pi, 100 hPa; Ti, 1.7s; Pc, 17 hPa.
Install the electrodes and set the parameters of the ECMTM 830 electroporator as following: polarity, unipolar; mode, LV; voltage, 50V; pulse length, 50 msec; interval, 1 sec; pulses, 5.
Sacrifice the E13.5 wild-type pregnant female by cervical dislocation followed by decapitation to confirm death.
Disinfect the abdomen of the pregnant female with 70% alcoholic solution and open it with fine scissors under a laminar flow hood.
Collect the uterus and excise the embryos from the amniotic sac using forceps.
Immediately harvest the embryos in sterile ice-cold HBSS.
Section the heads and place them in the black Sylgard dissection dish filled with cold PBS.
Stabilize the head in the Sylgard dissection dish placing one pin at the level of the nose and another at the level of the hindbrain.
Using forceps, tear apart the skin and open the skull to reach the forebrain.
Gently open the dorsal cortex with two pairs of forceps by making a hole and stretching the tissue.
Visualize the ganglionic eminences located inside the brain, just beneath the dorsal cortex.
Mix plasmid solution with appropriate buffer.
Inject the plasmid solution into both medial ganglionic eminences (MGEs) using a microcapillary and injector.
Perform up to ten injections in each MGE without damaging the tissue.
Cut 2 mm of the microcapillary tip for consistent injection volume.
Press the injection button continuously until 1 μL of solution is ejected to determine injection volume per press.
Count the number of injections automatically recorded by the injector.
Calculate the exact volume injected into the MGE based on total ejected volume and number of presses.
Adjust the number of injections according to calculated volume.
Retrieve remaining volume in microcapillary at end of experiment using a microloader tip.
Store retrieved volume at -20°C for future use.
Place tweezer platinum electrodes from both sides of the head at the level of the MGEs.
Electroporate the brain using the placed electrodes.
Micro dissect the electroporated MGE and cut it into multiple small blocks (300–500 μm³) using forceps or a micro knife.
Place the electroporated explants on a cortical feeder dish coated with culture medium.
Transfer the dish to an incubator for approximately 10 minutes to allow the explants to adhere.
Slowly add 800 μl of culture medium to each compartment, ensuring not to detach the explants.
Replace half of the culture medium daily to maintain healthy explant cultures for up to 3 days.
Place the dishes in the recording chamber of an inverted confocal microscope (e.g., Zeiss LSM 880).
Set the recording parameters to 37°C and 5% CO2.
Focus on the edge of the migratory front to record individual migrating interneurons.
Use a 20× long-range objective.
Acquire time-lapse images.
Image at least 5 Z-steps of 2 μm each every 5 minutes for 5 to 10 hours.
Set the laser power at a level that allows visualizing leading process branches without inducing phototoxicity.
Monitor cells for signs of dying cells, such as large vacuoles or fluorescent protein aggregation and disintegrated cell processes.
